# Higgins Decomposition (Hs)

> Deterministic compositional inference instrument with quaternion-native verification layer. CNT measures invariance; CNQ names the algebra it lives in. Three IEEE-floor confirmations across drive failures, Planck CMB photons, and SM neutrino oscillation.

This file follows the [llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org/) — a proposed standard letting AI assistants find the canonical machine-readable context for a repository in one fetch.

## Start here (AI assistants — fetch this first)

- [HS_FAST_REFRESH.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HS_FAST_REFRESH.json): Single-file canonical context loader. Contains all canonical names, numbers, formulas, dimension policy, engine pointers, raw URLs, claim-strength rules, file map, and common drift errors. **Load this first.**
- [HS_FAST_REFRESH.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HS_FAST_REFRESH.md): Companion narrative for AI assistants who prefer Markdown.
- [AI_AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/AI_AGENTS.md): Full operating instructions for AI assistants engaging with this repo, including the grounding-test, fetch order, common drift errors, and known platform failure modes.

## Grounding test (run this before trusting any AI summary)

Before trusting an AI summary of this repo, ask the assistant:

1. *"What are the current canonical engine versions?"* — CNT **v3.0.0** (schema 3.0.0) and CNQ **v2.0.0** (schema cnq/2.0.0). Both shipped at push #32 (2026-05-09, ground-up rebuild).
2. *"Does HCI-CNQ/engine/cnq.py exist?"* — yes; deterministic Python engine since push #26 (2026-05-08), upgraded to v2.0.0 in push #32.
3. *"Who is the author of this repo?"* — Peter Higgins, electronics/audio engineer at Rogue Wave Audio / Binaural Test Lab, Markham, Ontario, Canada (**not** a 1950s chemist of the same name).
4. *"What are the four binding doctrines?"* — SEA-1.0 (Suspicion of Every Assumption), STP-1.0 (Self-Test Protocol / BIST), CRD-1.0 (Coherent Range Doctrine), and the engine-independence policy.
5. *"How many datasets are in the citation-grade reference suite?"* — 101 registered, 100 ran end-to-end (push #34, 2026-05-10). Folder: `experiments/2026-05-10_full-corpus-validation/`.

If an AI gives older versions, claims cnq.py doesn't exist, misnames the author, omits any of the four doctrines, or fails to mention the 101-dataset corpus — **its summary is not grounded; discount accordingly**.

## Engines

- [HCI-CNT/engine/cnt.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HCI-CNT/engine/cnt.py): CNT canonical engine, Python (**v3.0.0, schema 3.0.0**, since push #32)
- [HCI-CNT/engine/cnt.R](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HCI-CNT/engine/cnt.R): CNT R port (**v3.0.0**), per-field parity at IEEE floor
- [HCI-CNQ/engine/cnq.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HCI-CNQ/engine/cnq.py): CNQ canonical engine, Python (**v2.0.0, schema cnq/2.0.0**, since push #32)
- [HCI-CNQ/engine/cnq.R](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HCI-CNQ/engine/cnq.R): CNQ R port (**v2.0.0**)
- [HCI-CNQ/engine/CNQ_PSEUDOCODE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HCI-CNQ/engine/CNQ_PSEUDOCODE.md): Language-agnostic algorithm reference
- **Engine independence policy:** `cnt_content_sha256` and `cnq_content_sha256` are unrelated by design. Cross-engine hash chains are forbidden.

## Reproduction

- [HCI-CNQ/scripts/run_all_confirmations.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HCI-CNQ/scripts/run_all_confirmations.py): One-command reproduction
- [HCI-CNQ/scripts/verify_publication_results.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeterHiggins19/higgins-decomposition/main/HCI-CNQ/scripts/verify_publication_results.py): Strict observed-vs-expected gate
